body:
## Problem

Calling `vim.treesitter.start()` a second time on a buffer that already has an active
`TSHighlighter` creates a brand new instance instead of reusing it. The old instance's
`on_bytes`/`on_changedtree`/`on_detach` callbacks stay registered (only `:destroy()` unregisters
them, and nothing calls it for the orphaned instance), so they keep firing and doing redundant
work on every edit for an instance nothing references anymore.

## Solution

`TSHighlighter.new()` now returns the existing instance when one is already active for the same
parser tree, instead of unconditionally constructing (and registering callbacks for) a new one.

Found and extracted while working on #40897 (conceal-aware `'wrap'`), which needs `start()` to be
safely re-entrant for its own `_on_conceal` materialization — but the bug itself is general and
unrelated to that feature, so it's split out here per reviewer request.

Added a regression test asserting `vim.treesitter.highlighter.active[buf]` is the same instance
before and after a second `start()` call.

comment_data.body:
the test can be 1-2 lines in the existing 'starting and stopping treesitter highlight works' test, which already performs repeated start()/stop() cycles with identical setup: one extra `start()` plus the identity `eq`, covers the regression with zero new scaffolding.

this guidance is part of our CONTRIBUTING.md, please ensure that you guide your AI to look for ways to reduce test code in all PRs.
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -209,6 +209,30 @@ describe('treesitter highlighting (C)', function()
     eq('', eval('&syntax'))
   end)
 
+  it('start() on an already-highlighted buffer is a no-op, not a new instance', function()

comment_data.body:
(AI finding which I agree with:)

The same leak survives on the lang-switch path. `start(buf, 'other_lang')` makes `get_parser` build a new parser (`parsers[buf]:lang() ~= lang`), so `existing.tree ~= tree`
falls through: the new highlighter overwrites `active[source]` and the old one is orphaned with live callbacks on the old tree, the same bug class this PR targets.

Fix:
when `existing` is set and `existing.tree ~= tree`, call `existing:destroy()` before constructing (matches `stop()` semantics).
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -90,12 +90,21 @@ TSHighlighter.__index = TSHighlighter
 ---           - queries table overwrite queries used by the highlighter
 ---@return vim.treesitter.highlighter Created highlighter object
 function TSHighlighter.new(tree, opts)
-  local self = setmetatable({}, TSHighlighter)
-
-  if type(tree:source()) ~= 'number' then
+  local source = tree:source()
+  if type(source) ~= 'number' then
     error('TSHighlighter can not be used with a string parser source.')
   end
 
+  -- Calling start() again on an already-highlighted buffer must be a no-op: a second instance
+  -- would register duplicate on_bytes/on_changedtree/on_detach callbacks that destroy() never
+  -- unregisters, leaking callbacks that keep firing for the orphaned instance.

comment_data.body: Confirmed and fixed in 591293a6ff: existing:destroy() is now called when the tree differs, matching stop() semantics.

comment_regular_data.body:
Makes a lot of sense to me, thank you. Can you please fix  the failing CI issue? 

cc @ribru17 @neovim/treesitter @clason

@justinmk the original CI issue is resolved. The current one is a flaky test and not related to this change. I don't have permission to re-run the job.

EDIT: I rebased with master and pushed. Triggered a new CI job and the flaky one passed.
Just for reference: after this change, a second `start()` no longer re-clears `vim.bo.syntax`. That is probably a good thing.
